mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.1% indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 0.1%.

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate exceeding 9.0% signals weak labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 9.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in GDP (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates robust economic demand that drives corporate profit expansion, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not positive in more than 60% of instances when GDPC1 growth > 0.5% quarterly and HOUST growth > 1% monthly.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production below 90 (INDPRO) signals manufacturing contraction that reduces business investment and corporate margins, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO < 90.

mechanism_narrative: CPIAUCSL above 220 indicates inflationary pressure that triggers Fed rate hikes, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuations for negative S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 220.

mechanism_narrative: Payroll growth exceeding 130,000 (PAYEMS) signals strong labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS > 130000.0.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent increases in retail sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicate strong consumer and housing demand that fuels economic growth and positive equity returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not positive in more than 60% of instances when RSAFS growth > 0.5% monthly and HOUST growth > 1% monthly.

mechanism_narrative: FEDFUNDS above 0.5% signals monetary tightening that increases cost of capital and reduces equity valuation multiples, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 0.5%.
